fields.v: Cheng, Y., Chen, H., Gao, P., Cheng, W. (2026). SpecForge: Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents via Behavioral Specifications. 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). arXiv:2610.15708v1 [cs.AI], 11 Oct 2026
Conference — NeurIPS 2026, 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (camera-ready footer on p. 1); read from arXiv:2610.15708v1 [cs.AI]
fields.why: Value did not follow the required form '<type> — <detail>'; type itself (Conference) was right.

fields.v: Virginia Tech (Y. Cheng, P. Gao); NEC Laboratories America (H. Chen, W. Cheng); first author's work done as NEC intern

Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — SpecForge, a multi-frontier tree search that refines per-entity behavioral specifications from execution feedback, compared against 5 groups of baselines (static docs, prompt optimizers, Cursor/Claude Code, iterative refinement, DocSearch) on 5 backbones on DevEval+, plus downstream transfer (Java translation, SWE-Dev)
fields.why: Form not followed, and the secondary nature was wrong: the draft named the revised DevEval+ benchmark (proposes an evaluation method), but DevEval+ is not listed among the contributions (p. 3) and is a revised release built to stress-test SpecForge (p. 7). The bulk of the study compares SpecForge with baselines.

fields.v: SpecForge (code github.com/ccsnow127/SpecForge; version Not stated). Baselines: RepoAgent, DocAgent (static docs); MIPROv2, GEPA, ACE (monolithic prompt optimization); Cursor and Claude Code (base, +Topo, +Test, +Topo+Test); Iterative, Iterative+Topo; DocSearch (same first authors, ICML 2026). Agent versions Not stated

Behavioral specification bundle: one natural-language specification per program entity (function/class/method: inputs, outputs, behavioral constraints); call graph; LLM-generated unit tests validated on the reference implementation (branch coverage >= 90%); Pareto archive of specification states

Initial specs from existing code -> loop (budget B = 50 rollouts): select archive state (Pareto, frequency-weighted) -> select eligible entity (callees solved, discounted-UCB) -> W = 3 refinements from different failing-test subsets (diagnosis + prescription prompts) -> regenerate full module code from specs only -> run tests -> update archive and bandit; return bundle with most resolved entities. Downstream: specs used for cross-language translation and new-feature implementation
None in the SpecForge loop (automatic, execution feedback). Commercial-agent +Test baselines ran with a budget of 50 manual action approvals; two authors verified the Java test translations
Full SpecForge loop (spec generation, code regeneration, test, refinement); downstream tasks use only the resulting specifications

Not classifiable (code is regenerated from the specifications alone, close to spec-as-source, but the specifications are recovered from existing code and judged by reconstruction rather than used to develop); authors' wording: 'behavioral specifications', 'specification-mediated recursive self-improvement'
fields.why: 'Not stated' is not a value of the form. The code-from-specs-only loop suggests spec-as-source, but the specs are reverse-engineered from a reference implementation, so 'not classifiable' is equally defensible.

fields.v: Existing code: specs derived from existing Python modules and judged by code reconstruction; downstream cross-language translation (Python to Java) and new-feature implementation in existing packages (SWE-Dev)

DevEval+: 20 Python modules, 247 entities, 760 tests, avg 12.4 entities/module, dependency depth 4.2 (max 10). DevEval+-Java: 16 modules, 208 entities, 680 tests. SWE-Dev: 10 packages, 27 instances (15 easy, 12 hard)
Diverse open-source Python modules (finance, NLP, bioinformatics, signal processing, scheduling, compilers, data validation, etc.)
N/A (no human participants)
Budget in rollouts (B = 50 spec->code->test cycles; baselines matched); convergence per rollout. No tokens, money or time reported. Compute: APIs from CPU desktops; Qwen on 8x H100
Solve rate |S| (share of entities passing all hidden ground-truth tests); pass rate (share of test cases passed); Pass@1 on SWE-Dev
None

Automatic: hidden ground-truth tests (never seen during search); search guided by LLM-generated tests (GPT-4o, temperature 0.7) validated on reference implementation; JUnit 5 harness for Java; SWE-Dev developer tests

Tasks: DevEval+ (20 modules) for the main comparison; DevEval+-Java and SWE-Dev subset for downstream transfer. Configurations: 11 methods/variants x 5 backbones (commercial agents only on supported models). Baselines: static docs, prompt optimizers, commercial agents, iterative refinement, DocSearch. Held constant: rollout budget (50) for optimizers, same LLM-generated test suite during search, hidden ground-truth tests for evaluation, backbone per column. Acceptance tests: hidden ground-truth tests. Repetitions: Not stated in body (checklist claims multiple seeds with mean/SD in appendix; not found). Human intervention: none in loop; up to 50 manual approvals for commercial-agent +Test

SpecForge best on all 5 backbones; +3.8 to +7.4 solve-rate points over DocSearch (avg +5.7), +3.6 to +6.6 pass rate; +23.5 to +49.1 points over best iterative baseline; Claude Code+Topo+Test and Cursor+Topo+Test trail by 33.0 and 42.8 points on Claude-4.5-Sonnet. Convergence: SpecForge 41% -> 93% pass rate over 50 rollouts while baselines oscillate. Transfer: Java +26.0 solve-rate points over Source-only; SWE-Dev beats benchmark PRD by +18.8 (easy) and +7.1 (hard). Significance: not tested

Distinguished methods clearly (large gaps), consistent across 5 backbones. Repeatability: code and data released; variance not reported in body. Limitations stated: loop requires a reference implementation; fixed search procedure; only 20 Python modules; DocSearch re-run on revised benchmark deviates 5.6 points from its original paper

Recursion is over specifications, not the improver (fixed search procedure); requires a reference implementation to validate self-generated tests; evaluation of the loop on 20 Python modules only, other languages only as downstream target. Execution-grounded feedback essential (LLM judge drops pass rate 19.6 points)

Code and data: github.com/ccsnow127/SpecForge. No pre-registration. Language: Python (Java downstream). Inconsistencies: checklist (p. 41) says experiments repeated across seeds with mean and SD in appendix, but no SD found; text says 'two' prompt optimizers adapted (p. 32) while three are compared; Claude Code* downstream runs on Claude-4.5-Sonnet while other downstream methods use GPT-4o. Author overlap: DocSearch (strongest baseline) is by the same first and senior authors. Table 1 values taken from p. 7 (extraction kept row order)

For the paper's own use cases (existing code) a reference implementation exists, so a reader could score Yes.
